title.narrative: Renforcement de la qualité de la formation initiale des paramédicaux en SSRAJ au Burundi

description.narrative:
Dans ce projet, CINOP, L’Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP), L’Université Lumière de Bujumbura (ULBU) et L'Institut Supérieur Paramédical de Gitega (ISPG) se fixent d'atteindre les résultats suivants:
1. Inclure les aspects de santé et droits sexuels et reproductifs y inclus la SSRAJ dans les curricula de la formation initiale des paramédicaux
2. Renforcer la capacité d’un noyau d’enseignants qui interviennent actuellement dans la formation initiale de ces paramédicaux pour reformater les curricula et disposer des compétences nécessaires pour donner ces cours
3. Elaborer un module de formation continue « Santé sexuelle et droits sexuels pour les adolescents et jeunes» pour les professionnels déjà en poste sur le terrain et qui est pilotée par les 3 institutions
4. Travailler avec les autres parties prenantes à une réelle harmonisation de la formation des paramédicaux et en particulier des Infirmiers, Sages-femmes, et agents de Santé Publique.
5. Signer une convention de collaboration entre les 3 bénéficiaires axée sur la formation des professionnels paramédicaux.This is a test from Akvo.

actual.value:
Despite the COVID pandemic that hampered its implementation, the project attained most of his prefixed results. This can detailed as follows:
- Output: Higher education institutions in Burundi have the capacity and promote better information and greater freedom of choice for young people about their sexuality
The three participating organisations have been capacited (developped curricula, trained staff, established partnerships (local public-private; internal networking); increased gender awareness) and are now in the position to effectively trains paramedics in the promotion of SHSR.
- Output:The partnership between the members of the Consortium (INSP, ULBU, ISPG and CINOP, UM) is sustainable and inclusive.
The following achievements have been reached: 1 Public-private partnership agreement exists between INSP, ULBU, ISPG and is functional; 2 collaboration contracts exist between the Burundian partners and the CINOP/UM Consortium The COVID pandemic did not allow strong (face-to-face) interactions during the past years. But project partners convened meetings to discuss collaboration when release of restrictions allowed to do so.
- INSP, ULBU and ISPG have strengthened their capacities in the training of paramedics for the promotion of SRHR and in particular SRHAY for the reduction of risk behaviors in the area of
sexual and reproductive health, including unwanted pregnancies and SGBV
Major milestones have been reached in relation to this output. These are the following: a core of 18 trainers (training of trainers) in SDSR with an emphasis on SRHAY (50% women) were trained within INSP, ULBU and ISPG; 7 additional staff were also trained that do not belong to the core group of trainers; 3 initial training curricula for paramedics (nurses, midwives, public health) harmonized and which include SDSR; 1 continuing education module in SRHR for professionals developed and piloted. The output has not been reached in full since the validation and subsequent implementation of the developped curricula await further actions from national authorities. Due to this situation, so far no student has been trained and benefited yet from the new initial training curriculum for paramedics integrating SRHR. We must first operationalize the SRHR modules and wait for the first cohorts of students to complete their courses and be in employment before being able to achieve these indicators. Nevertheless, the continuing education module SRHR has been piloted. This pilot took place as closing activity of the project. During this pilot, recommandations were made by the participants, the leadership of INSP and the Dutch embassy in Bujumbura for textual adjustments of the curricula before submission for approval to the national authorities. A follow-up has been given to these recommandations. INSP, ISPG and ULBU can now reach out to the Burundian validating bodies.

The project is ongoing. The development of the module SHSR is progressing. The level of achievement is around 70%. All undertaken activities were related to curriculum development. The most important milestones is the harmonisation of the programmes for the BAC I. If ressources are available, the next milestones will be the finalisation of the harmonisation process to include BAC II and BAC III.
